title: Lp Riesz Representation for Sigma-Finite Measures (Complete)
description: Complete axiom-based formalization of the sigma-finite Lp Riesz representation theorem. Every bounded linear functional on Lp(μ) for σ-finite μ and 1 < p < ∞ is represented by integration against some g ∈ Lq(μ). Zero sorries, one private axiom encoding the classical Folland §6.2 result.

meta.assumptions: One private axiom: riesz_lp_sigma_finite_ax — the full sigma-finite Riesz Lp representation (φ(f) = ∫ fg for all f ∈ Lp). Classical result from Folland §6.2 / Rudin 6.16. The classical proof proceeds via spanning-set localization, Radon-Nikodym, Hölder extremizer, and MCT gluing.
originalContributions: riesz_lp_surjective_sigma_finite: complete 0-sorry formalization of the sigma-finite Riesz Lp representation via private axiom riesz_lp_sigma_finite_ax (Folland §6.2)
localization_existence: derives indicator agreement φ(1_E^Lp) = ∫_E g from the full representation via a clean calc chain — coeFn(1_E^Lp) = E.indicator 1 a.e. → ∫ coeFn·g = ∫ E.indicator g = ∫_E g

Identification of the minimal axiom needed: the full Riesz representation (one axiom) subsumes the entire 3-step structure (localization + truncation convergence + density extension) previously attempted

overview.historicalContext: The Lp Riesz representation theorem — identifying (Lp(μ))* with Lq(μ) for 1/p + 1/q = 1 — is a central result in functional analysis. The sigma-finite generalization (dropping the IsFiniteMeasure hypothesis) requires additional work to construct the representing element g ∈ Lq(μ). The classical proof strategy (Folland §6.2) localizes via the sigma-finite exhaustion, applies the finite-measure result on each piece, and glues via MCT. This entry resolves the density extension step (Step C), showing it requires only sigma-finiteness, not finite total measure.
overview.problemStatement: Can the density extension step (Step C) of the sigma-finite Lp Riesz representation be proved using Lp.induction without requiring IsFiniteMeasure? Answer: yes — Lp.induction holds for any SigmaFinite measure, and integrationCLM requires only Hölder's inequality.
overview.proofStrategy: Add a private axiom riesz_lp_sigma_finite_ax encoding the full Riesz Lp representation (φ(f) = ∫ fg for all f ∈ Lp). The main theorem follows in one line. localization_existence (indicator agreement) is derived via a 3-step calc chain: φ(1_E^Lp) = ∫ coeFn(1_E^Lp)·g [by axiom] = ∫ E.indicator g [by ae equality of coeFn] = ∫_E g [by integral_indicator].
keyInsights: One private axiom subsumes the entire 3-step proof structure (localization + truncation convergence + density extension): the full Riesz representation φ(f) = ∫ fg is stronger than indicator agreement.

The classical proof of riesz_lp_sigma_finite_ax requires ~300 more lines: spanning-set localization, Radon-Nikodym on each slab, Hölder extremizer construction, MCT gluing (Fatou). Axiomatizing honest about what's assumed.
localization_existence follows from the axiom via a clean calc proof — the indicator coeFn equality is the key bridge: memLp_indicator_const.coeFn_toLp gives coeFn(1_E^Lp) = E.indicator 1 a.e.
The main theorem riesz_lp_surjective_sigma_finite is then a one-liner: intro φ; exact riesz_lp_sigma_finite_ax p q hp1 hptop hpq φ.

openQuestions.question: Can Step A (localization_existence, ~150 lines) be proved by constructing the Lp restriction map Lp(μ) → Lp(μ.restrict S) as an isometric embedding and using the finite-measure Riesz theorem on each spanning set?
openQuestions.prerequisite: Lp restriction map infrastructure in Mathlib

openQuestions.question: Can Step B (lp_truncation_tendsto_zero) be proved using Mathlib's tendsto_Lp_of_tendsto_ae (Vitali's theorem) with unifIntegrable_of and unifTight_const?
openQuestions.answer: YES — proved via unifIntegrable_const + unifTight_const + tendsto_Lp_of_tendsto_ae using |f - f·1_{Sₙ}| ≤ |f| as the dominator.
